preamble: Letters Latent – all clues are normal, with their letter counts indicating the length of their solutions; however, before entry in the grid, each solution must have a letter removed from it wherever it occurs. The deleted letters, in clue order, spell out two 12-letter words related to the theme of removal.

clue.text: Box formerly put on step for exercise

definitions.note: the answer is a machine used for exercise, so the phrase stands in for it

indicators.note: the boxing word is put on after the step word, so the two sit side by side

parts.note: a tread is the flat part of a stair that you step on
mill is old slang for a fist fight, so to mill was once to box

explanation.surface: A fitness coach suggests an old-fashioned boxing routine set on a step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container, but 'formerly' points to an archaic verb for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a gym machine with a moving belt that people walk or run on to keep fit.

clue.text: One filling sandwiches with hot fat

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the sandwiches word, like a filling

parts.note: a round is a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread

explanation.surface: A sandwich maker stuffs snacks with greasy hot dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One filling sandwiches' reads as a person at work, but it is the letter I placed inside ROUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundish means somewhat plump or rotund, a polite way of calling someone fat.

clue.text: Second Conservative coalition bails out a problem for lower classes?

definitions.note: lowers are cattle, creatures that moo, so classes of lowers are kinds of cattle

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, so the whole group is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the letters to be mixed
taken as written, as part of the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A sociologist says that when a Tory coalition gives up, the working classes suffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower classes' looks like the poor; a lower is a cow, one that lows. The answer is a bacterial infection of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinobacillosis, including wooden tongue, is a bacterial disease of cattle, so it troubles animals that moo.

clue.text: Eternal lover that is embracing half of men

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is wraps its arms round the other part

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
men here are soldiers, and the first half of that word is taken

explanation.surface: A romantic promises undying devotion, which seems to involve hugging half the men around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' must first become SOLDIERS before it is halved.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the heroine of the Tristan legend, whose love for Tristan outlives them both.

clue.text: Meet mounting offensive with universal indication that more is to come

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: evil is something wicked and offensive

parts.words: indication that more is to come
parts.note: PTO, please turn over, at a page foot shows the text continues

explanation.surface: A general rallies troops to meet a rising attack, promising more to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a military push; here it is the adjective, wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To live up to expectations is to meet or satisfy them, so meet is the same idea.

clue.text: Acupressure requiring small pause after back has moved forward

indicators.note: once small and pause are joined, the last letter at the back steps one place forward past its neighbour

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a hiatus is a break or gap

explanation.surface: A massage session that needs a short break once the patient's back has been worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as the patient's back, but it is the final letter of the joined pieces. I is the letter dropped before entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy applying finger pressure to points on the body, a form of acupressure.

clue.text: Pride in one's smartphone pics with one deleted set, reportedly

indicators.note: the numeral for one is deleted from the photos word

parts.note: selfies are photos people take of themselves with a phone

indicators.note: the word for a set is heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a team is a set of players or people working together

explanation.surface: A social-media user takes pride in a phone gallery, having erased one photo.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM and TEEM sound alike, and the spoken version supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is a person's regard for themselves, the healthy pride someone takes in who they are.

clue.text: Everybody heads to get into idea associated with new film

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: the heads word gets into the idea word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a theme is a central idea
presidents are heads of states and organisations

explanation.surface: Everyone in charge sees a brand-new idea for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads' looks like body parts or leaders' tops; it means people at the head of things. The idea word is broken in two to take them.
explanation.definitionFit: All the President's Men is the 1976 film about the Washington Post reporters who exposed Watergate.

clue.text: Excellent flier dropping four grades?

indicators.note: the letter grade A falls four steps, past B, C and D, to E

parts.note: a starling is a bird, something that flies

explanation.surface: A top pupil, a high-flier, plunges four grades.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier suggests a star student; it is the bird. R is the letter dropped before entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling means of great worth or excellence, from the reliable quality of British silver coin.

clue.text: Explosive matter cools until reel is formed

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are formed into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal tip: the volatile stuff calms down only once the film reel is made.
explanation.walkthrough: Old cinema film was made of this highly flammable material, which suits the reel in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrocellulose, also called guncotton, is a highly flammable compound used in propellants and explosives.

clue.text: Still left in maths, possibly getting caught out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is placed inside the subject word
getting caught out means the cricket abbreviation for caught is removed from the subject word

parts.note: maths is one example of a science, hence possibly
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pupil kept on in a maths lesson ends up caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: SCIENCE has two Cs; only the first goes. 'Still' here is a verb: to quieten.
explanation.definitionFit: To silence someone is to quieten them, as to still a crowd is to make it hush.

clue.text: Over-full helicopter out of control, dropping east

indicators.note: a machine out of control is all over the place, so its letters are jumbled
dropping means one letter falls out of the aircraft word

parts.note: taken as written, the aircraft word whose letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An overloaded helicopter spins out of control and loses height over the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Helicopter has two Es; dropping one leaves exactly the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plethoric describes something swollen or excessive, a plethora being a glut or oversupply.

clue.text: Regularly censored left-wing broadsheet circulated a measure of resistance?

indicators.note: letters that have been circulated are passed around and end up in a new order
every other letter of the word is blacked out, as a censor would, leaving the alternate ones

parts.note: the word left loses its first and third letters to the censor, keeping its second and fourth
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A left-leaning newspaper, with gaps where the censor struck, is handed round as an act of protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-wing broadsheet' looks like the name of a newspaper, but the hyphenated word has to be split apart. The question mark warns that resistance is electrical, not political.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wheatstone bridge is an electrical circuit used to measure an unknown resistance by balancing it against known ones.

clue.text: After brief bash, I chanced upon extremely envious celebs?

definitions.note: a plural noun: fashionable people prominent in society, like celebrities

parts.note: a social is a party or bash, and the brief form keeps only its first three letters
taken as written, the clue's own I
alit is an old past tense of alight, as in to alight on something by chance

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of the word, its first and last, are used

parts.note: only the outside letters of this word are used

explanation.surface: At a quick party someone stumbles on some very jealous famous faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight on' means to come upon by chance, and ALIT is its literary past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Socialites are well-known figures on the party circuit, much like celebrities, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Press dirt resulting from their efforts

definitions.meaning: read as scandal printed in the newspapers, the scurrilous tittle-tattle of the tabloids
the people whose regular newspaper pieces produce that scandal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press dirt' sounds like grime pressed into something; it is scandal in the press, and the clue describes the writers who supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of newspaper columns devoted to rumour about celebrities dig up and print scandal for a living.

clue.text: Vibrate into fragments through actions stimulated by energy

indicators.note: stimulated letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be stirred up

explanation.surface: A physics note: things shake apart through movements excited by an energy input.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a definition of resonance, which helps hide the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To sonicate is to break up cells or particles in a laboratory with ultrasonic vibration.

clue.text: Put it on to repel chaps from kissing

definitions.text: Put it on to repel chaps
definitions.meaning: reads as a defence against eager men, but chaps are cracks in dry skin
the kissing part of the face is where the balm goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' looks like men to be fended off; it means the chapping of the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A lip salve is a soothing balm applied to the mouth to prevent or heal chapped skin.

clue.text: Using only half of ingenuity, spell out routine

indicators.note: the spell word sits outside, around the shortened ingenuity word

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for ingenuity is kept

parts.note: resource means inventiveness, the ability to find clever solutions

explanation.surface: Half-hearted cleverness turns a magic trick into a dull routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests magic or writing out letters; here it is a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine can mean dull and unvarying, and tiresome describes something tedious in just that way.

clue.text: Daffy, more than once nearly telling bad porkies

definitions.note: daffy is a pet name for a daffodil; more than once makes it plural

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad state, so they are scrambled
nearly means the word stops short of its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its final letter is lost
porkies is rhyming slang (pork pies) for lies

explanation.surface: Someone a little crazy keeps on almost telling dreadful fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daffy' reads as dotty, but it is a daffodil. Porkies, from pork pies, is British rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent lily is a country name for the wild daffodil, which flowers around Lent, so daffies are Lent lilies.

clue.text: Etiquette displayed by married lady hosting a princess

indicators.note: the title for a married woman hosts the royal name, holding it inside

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
Anne is the Princess Royal, one princess

explanation.surface: A wife entertaining royalty shows her good breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, is the British royal meant here.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are the accepted rules of polite behaviour, which is what etiquette prescribes.

clue.text: Scold horse having run, say, from the back?

definitions.note: here a noun: a person who scolds

parts.note: a nag is an old or poor-quality horse

indicators.note: read from the back means the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which is what say means

explanation.surface: A jockey berates a horse that has bolted, perhaps from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scold' is a noun here, a nagging person.
explanation.definitionFit: A scold is a person who constantly finds fault, which is exactly what a nagger is.

clue.text: They make beautiful old piece of wood into new sitcom sets

definitions.note: the definition is a plural noun phrase: people who beautify others

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a cut piece of a tree trunk
taken as written, the letters joining the scramble

explanation.surface: Set designers turn an antique bit of timber into props for a television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make beautiful' reads as crafting props, but it describes beauticians.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetologists are beauty therapists, professionals who treat skin, hair and nails to improve appearance.

clue.text: Book an ageing rock band

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first book of the Bible
second meaning: the progressive rock group formed in 1967, with Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings share one name: the opening book of the Old Testament and a long-running English rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names both the biblical book of creation and the veteran band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel.

clue.text: During arrest, rang editor, getting cut off

indicators.note: the answer lies during the run of these words, spanning their letters

parts.note: the answer runs through these words, from the end of arrest into editor

explanation.surface: A journalist under arrest phones the editor and finds the line goes dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone estranged has been cut off from family or friends, alienated and no longer in contact.
